Crown browse by type volume/amplification amplification treble booster browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal Crown Fuzz and Treble Booster Published on April 6, 2020 Crown fuzz treble boost pedal Information The Crown Fuzz and Treble Booster is an early version of Applied Audio Products Inc.'s classic two-in-one fuzz and high-frequency boost design, manufactured in New Jersey during the late 1960s. Sold under multiple brand names including Goya, Giulietti, Sano, and Lou Rose, the Crown version represents one of the first commercially distributed OEM examples of this circuit. It combines a transistor-based fuzz effect with an independent treble booster, offering players the option of thick, saturated fuzz tones or bright, cutting lead sounds in a single compact pedal. The fuzz section produces a gritty, aggressive distortion with strong midrange and harmonic texture, while the treble booster enhances clarity and bite, particularly effective for rhythm work or for driving amplifiers into natural overdrive. The two effects can be used individually or together, providing a wide tonal range characteristic of early American fuzz pedals. Built with handwired, point-to-point construction and featuring heavy-duty metal housing, the Crown Fuzz and Treble Booster reflects the robust build quality of Applied Audio's designs. Early examples include an oversized battery test lamp and on/off pot for the treble circuit, both features that appeared on the earliest Goya and Lou Rose models. The control layout and component choice mirror those of other Applied Audio units, confirming a shared production lineage and marking this as one of the earliest iterations of the company's signature fuzz platform. sources.description: 136 likes, 15 comments - croytone_audio on October 16, 2024: "After more than a year of preparation, opening a shop in a new country and navigating the challenges of doing all of this in a language I am not very good at, I am extremely excited to announce the release of the first three effects pedals from the new CroyTone Audio Technologies Japan!!!! A ton of work went into these three fuzz pedals and I am extremely proud of the result! The Camper Fuzz, Hae Fuzz and Suzumebachi Fuzz are three distinct flavors of everything I love about fuzz pedals. The Camper Fuzz is the third iteration of my very first circuit I designed back in 2016. Everything I love about vintage style fuzzes in a more consistent and versatile package. From buzzy 60s fuzz tones to loud and heavy 70s sounds, the Camper Fuzz can do it all and more! The Hae is a continuation of an octave fuzz circuit I have been working on for years. Loud, brash and cutting, this fuzz can do all the screaming tones I love about 80s and 90s alternative and shoegaze fuzz. Strong octave and ring mod type tones are available with lots of tonal flexibility and PLENTY of volume. The Suzumebachi Fuzz is a newer design that comes from my love of stacking fuzzes to get a HUGE and thick fuzz tone. Massive doomy wall of sound fuzz tones are available as well as spitting, percussive gated tones. I’m so happy to finally get these out into the world and will begin shipping them out next week. Free shipping on all three pedals in Japan and the US! Available for purchase on my website! And thank you to the amazing @ryejol for designing the artwork on these pedals!".

sources.description: 136 likes, 15 comments - croytone_audio on October 16, 2024: "After more than a year of preparation, opening a shop in a new country and navigating the challenges of doing all of this in a language I am not very good at, I am extremely excited to announce the release of the first three effects pedals from the new CroyTone Audio Technologies Japan!!!! A ton of work went into these three fuzz pedals and I am extremely proud of the result! The Camper Fuzz, Hae Fuzz and Suzumebachi Fuzz are three distinct flavors of everything I love about fuzz pedals. The Camper Fuzz is the third iteration of my very first circuit I designed back in 2016. Everything I love about vintage style fuzzes in a more consistent and versatile package. From buzzy 60s fuzz tones to loud and heavy 70s sounds, the Camper Fuzz can do it all and more! The Hae is a continuation of an octave fuzz circuit I have been working on for years. Loud, brash and cutting, this fuzz can do all the screaming tones I love about 80s and 90s alternative and shoegaze fuzz. Strong octave and ring mod type tones are available with lots of tonal flexibility and PLENTY of volume. The Suzumebachi Fuzz is a newer design that comes from my love of stacking fuzzes to get a HUGE and thick fuzz tone. Massive doomy wall of sound fuzz tones are available as well as spitting, percussive gated tones. I’m so happy to finally get these out into the world and will begin shipping them out next week. Free shipping on all three pedals in Japan and the US! Available for purchase on my website! And thank you to the amazing @ryejol for designing the artwork on these pedals!".

Tone control adjustment was included for shaping the overall sound character. The AD-02 used the wedge-shaped enclosure style found throughout the C.S. Series, with geometric panel graphics and a top-mounted three-knob control layout. Like other pedals in the series, the AD-02 incorporated a switched volume control together with a two-stage battery conservation system connected to the input jack arrangement. The pedal operated from two 9 V "006P" batteries, with the series promoted for stable operation during performance use. Almost everything here is available off the shelf—nothing is custom made. The pedals include a Fulltone Clyde wah pedal, a Digitech Whammy controlled by a Molten Voltage MIDI 2 pedal, a Molten Voltage OZ Looper controller (no doubt controlling the Strymon Timeline, a Klon and Hot Cakes overdrives, a vintage CSL Super Fuzz (a/k/a Sola Sound), an Eventide H9, a Diamond Tremolo, a Dinosaural compressor, an MXR Flanger, a volume pedal and an Electro-Harmonix Deluxe Memory Man.
